insights.concise_text: Directly fine-tuning neural networks pretrained as language models to predict ERP components overcomes prior work's limitation of linking language models only to the N400 and P600.

triple.subject: neural networks pretrained as language models and fine-tuned to directly predict ERP components
triple.object: prior work linking language models to the N400 and P600

insights.concise_text: Because prior work used a linking function such as surprisal, its interpretable approach may have lost information that the direct-prediction model uses to predict all six ERP components.

triple.subject: linking function such as surprisal
triple.object: information available for predicting all six ERP components

insights.concise_text: The direct-prediction approach predicts a significant proportion of variance for all ERP components but loses the interpretability provided by a linking function.

triple.subject: direct-prediction approach
triple.object: loss of interpretability provided by a linking function

insights.concise_text: The finding that an LSTM can predict the P600 contrasts with BIBREF7, where LSTM surprisal was not significant in a mixed effects regression predicting the P600.

triple.subject: an LSTM predicting the P600
triple.object: LSTM surprisal in BIBREF7 mixed effects regression

insights.concise_text: Multitask learning benefits ERP prediction and suggests component relationships, but these joint-training benefit relationships remain only suggestive until verified across multiple datasets and neural network architectures.

triple.subject: verification across multiple datasets and neural network architectures
triple.object: interpretation of joint-training benefit relationships

insights.concise_text: Using heterogeneous data in multitask learning is a potentially major advantage because human language processing datasets are small and information can be shared between behavioral and neural data.

triple.subject: small datasets associated with human language processing
triple.object: heterogeneous data to be a potentially major advantage of a multitask approach

insights.concise_text: The six ERP components analyzed from BIBREF0 include semantic markers N400, EPNP, and PNP and syntactic markers P600, ELAN, and LAN, all predicted above chance by the fine-tuned model.

triple.subject: fine-tuned model
triple.object: six ERP components from BIBREF0

insights.concise_text: Because EEG has temporal resolution for meaning integration and ERPs are identified with comprehension processes, predicting ERP components can probe features mediating human language comprehension.

triple.subject: predicting ERP components
triple.object: EEG study of meaning integration to probing human language comprehension

insights.concise_text: The caution about varying neural network architectures is supported by appendix variants using only the forward-encoder or only word embeddings, which produced clearly worse results than a bi-LSTM encoder.

triple.subject: forward-encoder and word-embeddings variants
triple.object: clearly worse results than using a bi-LSTM encoder

insights.concise_text: ERP components can cancel and mask each other, which complicates interpreting the shared information between ERP components found through multitask learning.

triple.subject: ERP components canceling and masking each other
triple.object: interpretation of shared information between ERP components
